गौरम्

GAURA(M) . A mountain in the kuśa island. (bhīṣma Parva, Chapter 12, Verse 4).

गौरमुख

GAURAMUKHA . A son of sage śamīka. It was Śamīka's son Śṛṅgī, who cursed parīkṣit to death by snake-bite. (See parīkṣit). Śṛṅgī cursed that parīkṣit, who had thrown a dead snake on the neck of his father while in meditation, would be bitten to death by snake within seven days. Śṛṅgī sent word about the curse through his disciple gauramukha to parīkṣit. (Ādi Parva, Chapter 42, Verses 14-22).

गौरप्रभ

GAURAPRABHA . Son born to śuka (Vyāsa's son) by his wife pīvarī. śuka had four sons called kṛṣṇa, gauraprabha, bhūri and devaśruta and a daughter kīrti. (devībhāgavata, Prathama skandha).

गौरपृष्ठ

GAURAPṚṢṬHA . A royal sage who worships yama at his sabhā (assembly). (Sabhā Parva, Chapter 8, Verse 21).

गौरशिरस्

GAURAŚIRAS . A sage of ancient days, who worshipped indra in his assembly. (Sabhā Parva, Chapter 7, Verse 11).

गौरवाहन

GAURAVĀHANA . A King, who was present at the rājasūya sacrifice of yudhiṣṭhira. (Sabhā Parva, Chapter 34, Verse 12).

गौरी २

GAURĪ II . A female attendant (devī) of pārvatī. (Vana Parva, Chapter 231, Verse 48).

गौरी ३

GAURĪ III . Wife of varuṇa. (Udyoga Parva, Chapter 117, Verse 9).

गौरी ४

GAURĪ IV . An Indian river. (bhīṣma parva, Chapter 9, Verse 25).

गौरीश

GAURĪŚA . A royal sage and a member of Yama's assembly. (Sabhā Parva, Chapter 8, Verse 18).

गौरीशिखरम्

GAURĪŚIKHARA(M) . A sacred place on the Himālayas. A bath in Sthānakuṇḍa here brings the same benefits as are derived from the performance of vājapeya and aśvamedha sacrifices. (Vana Parva, Chapter 84, Verse 151).
